newsitem.title: USA: US utilities in West call for power grid operator.
newsitem.headline: US utilities in West call for power grid operator.

text.p: Electric utilities in the Western United States continue to call for the formation of one or more regional independent system operators (ISOs) as a means of improving reliability of the western power grid.

At a U.S. Congressional subcommittee hearing today in Los Angeles, several utilities and power agencies repeated calls for mandatory compliance with reliability standards, saying centralization of transmission operation is needed.
The subject of the hearing was the blackout which hit the West August 10.

Vikram Budhraja, senior vice president for power grid operations at Edison International's Southern California Edison Co, said, "ISOs will increase reliability by focusing responsibility within a single organization, simplifying communications and cooordination."
California has already provided for a statewide ISO under a law which phases in competition in the electric power industry starting January 1998.
The Bonneville Power Administration, the federal agency which markets electricity from the Northwest, also endorsed mandatory compliance with reliability standards and the formation of ISOs.
Randy Hardy, Bonneville's administrator, emphasized that authority to schedule, as well as dispatch power should rest with a single regional system operator.
The Western System Coordinating Council (WSCC), an industry group which oversees the grid, said it is imperative to segment power generation from transmission.
Mark Bonsall, WSCC chairman, said existing reliability councils across the United States should be retained and possibly expanded.

James Macias, vice president of electric transmission at Pacific Gas and Electric Co, said, "Organizational separation of the ISO from...other supply coordinators will ensure a reliability-only focus."
